svg.text: Hook chain — what fires on which event, and which arm blocks
Two registration channels carry the walls, and a guard keeps exactly one of them live per event. Every entry is rooted at ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} and runs with timeout: 10.
ALWAYS ON
payload/hooks/hooks.json — installed with the plugin, live in every session on the machine, whether or not the skill was ever invoked.
EVENT
WHAT RUNS
ARM
WHAT IT STOPS
PreToolUse · Bash
protect-main.sh
BLOCK · exit 2
A git push to main or master. The command is split on && / || / ; and only real command segments are read, so a
commit message that happens to mention pushing is not a hit. The user pushes to main from their own terminal.
PreToolUse · Bash
protect-database.sh
BLOCK · exit 2
DROP, TRUNCATE, ALTER TABLE … DROP, and a DELETE with no WHERE — through psql, mysql, sqlite3 and the
other common database CLIs.
PreToolUse · Agent
agent-context-guard.sh
→ dispatch-preflight.sh
BLOCK · exit 2
A dispatch, during an active wave, with no this-session environment attestation — or whose brief names no single
Expected artifact: path (zero refuses to name one, more than one refuses to choose). Outside a wave: untouched.
PreToolUse · Write
agent-context-guard.sh
→ canonical-sdlc-governing-skill.sh
BLOCK · exit 2
An artifact under <docs-root>/{specs,plans,adrs,incidents}/ that fails the ladder below — the full frontmatter
contract, plus the three-way design rule on a wave-or-epic spec.
PreToolUse · Edit
agent-context-guard.sh
→ canonical-sdlc-governing-skill.sh
BLOCK · exit 2
The same wall, reached on the Edit path — but it validates Write CONTENT only, so one valid write covers every
later edit of that file. A known hole, listed again at the bottom of this page rather than left to be discovered.
SubagentStop
agent-context-guard.sh
→ landing-gate.sh
BLOCK · once
The landing sweep, reached from inside an agent context. It refuses the stop exactly once if a contract that has
landed since the last sweep named artifacts that are not on disk, then lets the next one through.
THE CHANNEL PARTITION — why the same wall is registered twice, and what keeps it from firing twice

A skill-frontmatter hook is looked up by SESSION id, and a tool event raised inside a subagent is dispatched under the AGENT id — so a wall registered on the skill channel is structurally invisible from inside an agent, which is

how delegation used to escape every wall this repo installed. The plugin channel above is alive in both places, so pointing it straight at a wall would double-fire on the main thread. It points at agent-context-guard.sh instead,

which execs the wall it was handed by argument only when (1) the payload carries a top-level agent_id — this is an agent context — and (2) .bionic/tmp/roster-<session_id>.state exists — this session is armed.
Anything else, ambiguity included, exits 0 in silence: the guard never refuses on its own account and never prints, because a refusal nobody wrote would be attributed to the wall standing behind it.
ARMED BY THE SKILL
the hooks: block in skills/canonical-sdlc/SKILL.md frontmatter — live on the main thread only while the skill is loaded, and gone when it is not.
EVENT
WHAT RUNS
ARM
WHAT IT DOES
PreToolUse · Bash
canonical-sdlc-evidence-gate.sh
BLOCK · exit 2
The commit wall — its ladder is below. It fires only on a real git commit segment (quote-aware), so every other
Bash command passes it untouched.
PreToolUse · Bash
farm-out-reminder.sh
DENY · via JSON
A long-running main-thread command — the full test suite, the bootstrap — is denied with a redirect naming the
role that should run it; fuzzy matches get one nudge per class per session. Exit 0 always: the decision is stdout JSON.
PreToolUse · TaskStop
stop-guard.sh
BLOCK · exit 2
A stop backed by no fresh observation, by a spent one, or by another actor's borrowed look — and a stop of a target
this session never launched, when addressed by name. The full agent id is the deliberate path past that refusal.
PreToolUse · Agent
dispatch-preflight.sh
BLOCK · exit 2
The start gate, reached on the main-thread channel — the same script lane A reaches through the guard. This is also
the arm that writes the session roster row, which is why the guard hands the agent-context copy a flag to skip it.
PreToolUse · Write, Edit
canonical-sdlc-governing-skill.sh
BLOCK · exit 2
The artifact wall, reached on the main-thread channel — one registration per matcher, the same script behind both,
and the ladder below is what it walks.
PostToolUse · Bash
execution-recorder.sh
RECORD
The observation arm. When stop-check.sh has run and printed its machine line, that line becomes the record a later
stop is allowed to spend — one observation, exactly one stop.
PostToolUse · Agent
execution-recorder.sh
RECORD
The roster arm. A dispatch that actually spawned completes its intended row with the full agent id and status
confirmed — the launch record that survives the conversation turning.
SubagentStart
execution-recorder.sh
RECORD
The identification arm. The agent's own transcript-form id joins the roster BY THAT ID — not by name, and not by
the payload's agent_type, which carries the subagent TYPE and made the join collide.
Stop
context-spend.sh
LOG ONLY
One context-spend line per SDLC step boundary. A missing jq, transcript, usage block or plan means exit 0 and
silence; it never writes stdout at all, because a Stop hook's stdout could be read as a block payload.
Stop
landing-gate.sh
BLOCK · once
The landing sweep at the orchestrator's own turn end: a verdict for every contract that has landed since the last
sweep, and one refusal if any of them named an artifact that is not on disk. Outside an active wave: untouched.
THE TWO SDLC LADDERS — first failure wins, and it names itself
canonical-sdlc-governing-skill.sh
PreToolUse · Write, Edit — the artifact wall
the path is under <docs-root>/{specs,plans,adrs,incidents}/
governing-skill: is present in the frontmatter
canonical_sdlc_version == 13
the triple is present and enum-valid — intent · rigor · scale
no mode: line, and the intent × scale cell is not barred
flags and model_plan present; walk: is required or exempt
## Verification Matrix present once sdlc-step ≥ 3
a wave-or-epic SPEC satisfies one design arm: a flush-left
## Design in place, a design: pointer that resolves to a file
carrying one, or a design-waived: token
All pass → the Write proceeds. Any failure → exit 2, and the file is
never written.
LOG-ONLY: rigor-floor consistency — and it logs user-overridden rather
than a violation when rigor-override: is present. Plans and task-scale artifacts are untouched.
canonical-sdlc-evidence-gate.sh
PreToolUse · Bash — the commit wall, on real git commit segments only
newest plan under the plan dirs → its ## SDLC State, fence-aware
canonical_sdlc_version == 13
current: N — or current: T<n> at scale: task
Step N's evidence keys present, and none of them a placeholder
(todo · pending · in progress · xxx · tbd · placeholder all reject)
at Step 5: cmd / pass / total / output with pass == total, a valid
## Verification Matrix, and a non-empty auditor: once no row is pending
from current: 5 onward — no AC block says provenance: implementation
from current: 5 onward — walk-artifact: resolves to a real file under
<docs-root>/record/ and names the AC, once any row is discharged
(unless the plan declares walk: exempt)
Valid → the commit proceeds. Otherwise → exit 2, and git never runs.
LOG-ONLY: the epic merge-target check, and the intent-scoped Step-5 keys
for refactor (behavior-preservation · compat-matrix · revert-plan) and tune (baseline · target · re-measure).
ONE SUPPORTED VERSION
canonical_sdlc_version: 13 is the only value either hook accepts.
Anything else — older, empty, malformed — exits 2 naming the value it
found. No dispatch chain, no ladder, no grandfathering. The hooks own
the number; this page's three renderings of it are pinned against them.
THE LOG-ONLY SIDE CHANNEL
$HOME/.claude/logs/<project-slug>/sdlc-audit.md
Deliberately outside every consuming project tree. One line per finding
plus an stderr echo, and it never blocks the wave. Promoting any of it to
blocking is a later decision, made by the user from this data.
KNOWN HOLES — NOT ENFORCEMENT
The governing-skill hook validates Write content, not Edit content: one
valid write covers every later edit. Flag VALUES are never checked, only
presence. The evidence gate reads the plan's text, so an Edit writing
evidence for tests never run passes unseen. Proof-shape is a heuristic.
